RSHUNT.reference: INA180 datasheet SBOS518, typical application with high-side sensing
RSHUNT.derivation: Vsense = I_max × Rs = 10A × 0.01Ω = 100mV. Within INA180 common-mode range, provides good SNR.

INA180_gain.derivation: Vout = Vsense × G. Need Vout < 3.3V at I_max=10A. With Rs=10mΩ: Vout = 10A × 0.01Ω × 25 = 2.5V < 3.3V ✓

R_VSENSE_H.derivation: Voltage divider ratio = R_L / (R_H + R_L) = 0.270 for 12V → 3.24V. Standard E12 values 27k and 10k give ratio 10/(27+10) = 0.270.

R_VSENSE_L.derivation: See R_VSENSE_H. Forms 0.270 divider ratio with 27kΩ upper resistor.

C_ISENSE_BYPASS.reference: INA180 datasheet SBOS518 § 8.2.1, power supply bypass capacitor
C_ISENSE_BYPASS.margin: Standard bypass value for op-amp ICs

C_ISENSE_FILT.reference: INA180 datasheet SBOS518 § 8.2.1, optional output filter
C_ISENSE_FILT.derivation: Reduces ADC input noise. Cutoff frequency with RP2040 ADC input impedance (~10kΩ) is fc = 1/(2π×10k×100nF) ≈ 160Hz, adequate for DC measurements.
C_ISENSE_FILT.margin: Filters switching noise while preserving DC accuracy

C_VSENSE_FILT.derivation: Low-pass filter with divider resistance: fc = 1/(2π×37kΩ×100nF) ≈ 43Hz. Removes switching noise.
C_VSENSE_FILT.margin: Slow enough to filter noise, fast enough for monitoring (23ms time constant)

R_OVP_PU.reference: LM393 datasheet SLCS161, typical pull-up for open-collector output

R_OVP_HYST.reference: TI app note SLVA863, comparator hysteresis design
R_OVP_HYST.derivation: Hysteresis = Vref × (R_pullup / R_hyst) ≈ 3.3V × (10k/100k) = 330mV ≈ 10% hysteresis prevents oscillation.
R_OVP_HYST.margin: PLACEHOLDER - needs sourcing, may use series 10kΩ resistors

R_LED.derivation: I_LED = (V_FB - V_LED) / R = (12V - 1.2V) / 10kΩ = 1.08mA. Lower than typical 5mA but adequate for PC817 CTR at 50-200%.
R_LED.margin: DEVIATION: 1mA instead of 5mA saves power, CTR still adequate

R_TEMP_TOP.derivation: Forms voltage divider with 10kΩ NTC thermistor. At 25°C (R_NTC=10k): V_mid = 1.65V. At 80°C (R_NTC≈1.5k): V_mid ≈ 2.87V.
R_TEMP_TOP.margin: Provides good voltage swing over operating temperature range

C_TEMP_FILT.derivation: Tau = R × C = 10kΩ × 10nF = 100µs. Fast enough for temperature (slow thermal constant), slow enough to filter electrical noise.
